items.evidence: The export coverage validator now receives md_narrative_text or '', eliminating the reported None.lower() failure. The failing-narrative integration test asserts successful document/report production. Tests could not run under Python 3.12. The new 'no claims' test is weaker than its name suggests: it supplies no transcript but still uses a populated manifest, allowing synthesized claims.

The post-polish loop restores fallback text, rejects capture rewrites failing round_trip_ok, checks lost text claims, and records reverted step IDs. All exporters consume the resulting md_step_results. Photo captions appropriately bypass the synthetic manifest's action check; transcript-backed photo fallback text remains protected. Added tests cover dropped element names and fallback preservation; existing polish tests use the new round-trip-capable stub. Runtime test results remain unavailable.

Captioned photo steps now receive narration, while caption failures retain transcript text without duplicating narration. Export polish restores photo narration. However, server.py:549 invokes semantic rescue, whose server.py:870 call to polish_narration rewrites the transcript before the new narration assignment. A read-only probe confirmed that 'okay open the console' -> 'Open the console.' passes that gate. Added verbatim tests cover deterministic placement, not this successful semantic rewrite.

regressions.title: New DPI initialization discards usable fallback APIs when an optional API is absent
regressions.evidence: All DLL loading and function-signature setup share one try block. Missing SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext or shcore causes _winapi to return neither handle, preventing the advertised older-Windows fallback sequence and leaving awareness dependent on later imports. A read-only probe reproduced 'unavailable' despite working fallback APIs. Existing injected-handle tests bypass this loader and miss the defect.
